records.mutation: replace vague 'intersect constraints across readings' with a constructive two-witness test for ignorance, and state that readings disagreeing on the pinned value is itself ignorance so a candidate refuted under one fixed reading survives
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent scored 0/8; 2 hit the 16384 cap and all eight burned 13k-16.4k tokens. Every rollout proved that under each fixed reading a speaker's own value pins the partner, declared both readings impossible, and then reported a factor or complement its own text had just refuted. One even reached the balanced split, said it forced knowledge, and reported a neighbour. So the binding error is not the ordering or the guessing ban but the criterion for ignorance itself: the student equates it with many partners inside one reading. I replaced the intersect-across-readings clause with a constructive test -- name two scenarios matching what the speaker was told but differing in the unknown -- and stated that two readings each pinning a DIFFERENT value already create ignorance, so a candidate refuted only under one fixed reading must be kept.

records.mutation: restate the opening move as the general homogeneity/equal-degree trigger for dividing to a single ratio and w^n=c, keeping the incumbent's second paragraph intact
records.subagent_summary: 7 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct in 5.8k-9.1k tokens. The single failure reached the correct locus and radius by 2.4k tokens, then mis-inverted a purely imaginary reciprocal while probing one root, and spent the remaining 14k tokens re-deriving the same sound algebra (60 restarts of reasoning, 9 claims of contradiction) until the cap with nothing recorded. Rounds 5-16 all rewrote the second paragraph to bound, redirect or replace that audit loop, and all twelve lost transfer, so the loop language is not the lever. The untouched lever is the opening move, which since round 4 has read as a bare recipe for this equation. I keep the second paragraph verbatim and restate the first as its transferable trigger: equal degree on both sides licenses dividing to a single ratio, giving w^n = c and a pinned modulus.

records.mutation: make the non-containment check computational: test each vertex of the pinned piece against the two edge inequalities at the corner, instead of a qualitative wedge claim
records.subagent_summary: Five of eight scored, so the sum-minus-overlap frame and trade test are kept. All three failures shared one error, not a budget problem: each asserted that the large piece's sides all sit at distance 1 from its center while the pinned piece only reaches 0.5, so containment holds at every rotation and the overlap equals the whole piece. One wrote that conclusion out confidently and stopped early with tokens to spare; the other two never closed reasoning, cycling 109-139 rotation retests around the same claim while repeatedly calling the geometry too complex to compute. The incumbent's qualitative wedge sentence and reference-point warning did not block it. This revision replaces them with a computational test: express the two edges leaving the pinned corner as inequalities and check each vertex of the other piece, so one failing vertex refutes containment numerically.

records.mutation: lead with a do-not-invent-constraints rule (reuse allowed unless forbidden; a whole-pattern condition need not hold piecewise) and an exit for impossible/unbounded branches, plus an agreement-count framing that pins the per-piece cap at the stated degree
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts: 3/8 correct. No truncation and no arithmetic slips - every loss came from a self-invented constraint. Two rollouts decided each piece may be used only once and reported the bare piece count; a third first argued the count was unbounded, then retreated to that same piece count as the "practical" choice. Two more applied the multiplied budget correctly in form but with a per-piece cap one below the degree stated in the problem, having subtracted the affine target and then differenced again. One stalled mid-derivation. So the incumbent needs less residual bookkeeping and more license discipline: state up front that reuse is permitted unless forbidden and that a whole-pattern condition need not hold piece by piece, give impossible/unbounded branches a one-line exit, and pin the per-piece cap by counting agreements with the line at the degree exactly as given.

records.mutation: swap the costly second-method verification for substitute-back checking, a no-re-verify stop, and a re-read-the-question step
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling gave 7/8 correct at 20-27k characters, the same score as the incumbent's recorded train_i, so train is near saturated and held-out (weighted double) is the only real lever. The lone failure derived the constants and the translation equation correctly, then wrongly threw away one of two roots on a botched domain check, accepted the resulting degenerate figure, and spent its remaining budget re-deriving the same shoelace sum instead of doubting the discard. Fifteen earlier rounds already tried rewriting the root-screening clause and every one lost held-out ground, so I left that clause untouched and instead replaced the expensive 'verify by a second, different method' instruction with cheap substitute-back checking, an explicit no-re-verification stop, and a re-read-the-question step so budget goes to the quantity actually requested.

records.mutation: make orientation mechanical (label the source pile, buffer releases top first) so the asked slot becomes an exact opening load block, and forbid overwriting a step-listed value with an unlisted symmetry claim
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling gave 2/8; seven rollouts stopped normally and one hit the cap relitigating, so length is secondary. Part (a) is mostly solved (five reached the free-step count), and every loss was the slot part: six asserted a uniform random permutation and read off 1/n or 3!/4!, each having first equated the deepest slot with 'moved last'. Two rollouts even derived the correct free-step value and then explicitly overwrote it with a symmetry story a paragraph later. Several also mislabelled the start pile orientation, so they named the wrong item. The revision makes orientation mechanical rather than a reading to pick, adds the buffer rule that an item leaves only after later entrants, converts the slot event into an exact opening block of loads, and forbids overwriting a step-listed value with an unlisted symmetry claim.

records.mutation: turn self-reported stalling into an explicit stop-and-commit trigger; ban restating the setup; require a third instance to distinguish growth types
records.subagent_summary: All eight fresh rollouts hit the generation cap and none emitted a result, so this round scored zero purely on budget exhaustion, not on reasoning ability. Every transcript spent its opening paragraphs re-paraphrasing the given conditions in new notation, then cycled through abstract framings, and several literally wrote that they were stuck or out of ideas and opened yet another approach instead of landing anything. Some had already computed correct small instances and still never committed. The incumbent asks for early commitment but gives no trigger for it, so the revision bans restating the setup, demands a written value from the smallest instance immediately, requires a third instance to separate factorial from power growth, and converts the model own stuck/how-do-I-proceed language into an explicit stop-and-commit deadline.

records.mutation: keep the train-safe opening and small-cases clause verbatim; replace the never-exercised exact-fractions clause with an untried candidate-screening rule (reject values violating positivity/integrality/range, re-test extraneous roots) plus an all-givens-used misread check
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 and stopped cleanly at 3.0-7.0k of 16384 tokens, so train_i is pinned at 1.0 and length is not the binding constraint; every remaining gain must come from transfer. The rollouts never once used the exact-fractions clause (all arithmetic is small-integer), so that clause is dead weight on transfer while occupying budget. What the rollouts do spend real effort on is enumerating divisor candidates and then arguing which survive the stated conditions, and they only converge after discarding the ones that conflict with a given. I generalized exactly that observed move into a reusable candidate-screening rule covering positivity, integrality, range limits and extraneous roots from squaring or clearing denominators, and added an all-givens-used check since misreads are the residual failure class. Screening and extraneous-root discipline are untried in prior rounds here.

records.mutation: forbid re-expansion into standard powers when reading off results and add a settled-value rule (a checked value outranks a later disagreeing rewrite), replacing the redundant same-sign/factor-out warnings
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling gave 3/8 correct, down from the incumbent's earlier 8/8, and the failures split cleanly. Four rollouts never adopted the centered form and burned all 16384 tokens matching coefficients of the degree-9 composition, chasing sign contradictions in their own expansions. The one rollout that terminated wrong had already recentered, pinned the center and scale correctly, and verified both supplied values, then re-expanded into standard powers, wrongly re-added the given constant on top of the center, distrusted its verified values, and overwrote them with the corrupted ones. The revision therefore keeps the recentering core but spends its tokens on the two live traps: evaluate only inside the centered form, and treat a value that already matched the data as settled so a later disagreeing rewrite is discarded instead of the value.

records.mutation: add an explicit sufficiency/stopping rule (agreeing cases are enough, no general proof owed) and make self-repetition or confusion a hard exit signal rather than a cue to restart symbolically
records.subagent_summary: 5 of 8 rollouts were correct and every one read the pattern straight off two or three literal small traces, then stopped. All 3 failures ran to the 16384-token cap, and none failed for lack of a correct case: each had already produced small-case values matching the eventual pattern, then discarded them as 'tedious' and switched to a symbolic product-of-permutations derivation. Two degenerated into verbatim repetition loops of one cycle expression; one drifted into a bogus larger count and hunted an unrelated integer sequence. So the binding constraint is no longer how cases get traced, since the incumbent's clause already works, but the absence of permission to stop once cases agree. The revision keeps the parameter-shape check and literal tracing, adds an explicit sufficiency rule (agreeing cases mean done, no general proof owed), and makes self-repetition or 'confusing' a hard exit.
